findings.description: The journey model makes consumer optional, but the objective requires declaring the intended consumer family for consumer-facing outcomes. If omission remains valid, typing and consumer-surface validation can be bypassed before close-time enforcement ever sees stable vocabulary.

The seeded evidence rule depends on fixture_only, but the plan only says fixture_only is optional and does not pin its default. Missing fixture_only semantics can make seeded_masks_readiness nondeterministic for older or partially-authored journeys.

The typing function is specified for one surface_class, but journeys can declare multiple surfaces and consumer=both. The plan does not pin journey-level aggregation semantics that require at least one human-surface requirement and at least one agent-surface requirement to be satisfied together.

The structured_error rule depends on a degraded or error-path claim, but claim_kind is otherwise closed to read_only, mutation, and qualitative. There is no pinned input field that tells the pure typing rule when an error path is being evaluated.

The mutation requirement notation is ambiguous: the prose says idempotency plus rollback are both required, but the requirement-expression example could be read as alternatives or as malformed grouping.

F004 says degraded_dishonest only when neither family provides availability=unavailable for a required data_source, but the user journey requires both human and agent families to degrade honestly. One family could silently omit its degraded signal while the other family masks the failure.

The checker needs to compare human and agent EvidenceRefs by data_source, but EvidenceRef does not gain an explicit surface_class, consumer_family, or source-family attribution field. Inferring family from evidence_class is underspecified and breaks for shared classes such as structured_error.

F004 adds allowed_degraded_modes to the contract but never specifies how the checker validates or consumes those modes. That leaves an accepted schema field with no behavioral effect in the honesty gate.

The CLI transcript adapter is required to be non-interactive and no live paid call may be made, but the plan does not pin the command contract, fixture mode, or environment guard that prevents accidental paid external execution.

The contract names the typed-skip reason-location fix as D028, while F003 labels the same acceptance point as D029. This drift can cause implementers to miss the exact round-3 typing fix the objective says is in scope.

F002 references a close gate named F005 even though close-time enforcement is explicitly out of scope and delegated to sibling plan 2b. This creates an implementation target that is not part of the objective contract.

F002 says satisfaction matches evidence_class plus data_provenance, while F004 says availability=unavailable typed-skips must never satisfy a consumer-surface capture. Without an explicit shared rule, a degraded typed-skip carrying the required evidence_class could be counted as satisfied by the typing checker.

F004 requires degraded EvidenceRefs to use an allowed degraded mode, but neither F001 nor F004 defines a structured field on EvidenceRef that carries the selected degraded mode. That leaves the checker unable to enforce allowed_degraded_modes without reading prose.

F001 makes consumer_family optional even though F004 depends on per-family degradation and cross-family agreement. If availability-bearing EvidenceRefs omit consumer_family, the checker cannot reliably prove that each required family degraded honestly.

The typing matrix is only partially pinned. F002 gives example requirements for several surfaces, but it does not explicitly define read_only requirements for every closed surface_class, including interactive_ui, mobile_app, external_integration, and service_batch.

The MCP adapter acceptance pins tools/list but leaves the second read-only tool as an example such as list_projects or status. That makes the dogfood fixture dependent on whatever tool happens to exist, weakening deterministic harness tests.

The plan adds new agent EvidenceSource adapters, but F004 also requires human-family unavailable labels with structured data_source, availability, provenance, and consumer_family. The non-goal excludes rebuilding human-surface capture, yet no minimal compatibility path is specified.

F001 requires a total SurfaceFamily mapping, but the proposed plan does not pin the exact family for every closed surface_class member. Ambiguous cells like external_integration, service_batch, and backend-derived surfaces can change consumer x surface validation outcomes.

The journey.surfaces token mapping named in F001 lists web, backend, mcp_tool, cli_agent, and cli_human, but does not pin tokens for mobile_app or external_integration even though those are closed surface_class values and mobile human capture already exists.

F002 states that agent_mcp_tool read_only success is satisfied by tool_call_transcript or contract_check, but the listed tests do not include the required unit-test-only mismatch and transcript-satisfied agent API/MCP cases from the journey contract.

F003 typed-skip EvidenceRefs specify availability=unavailable and data_provenance=degraded, but do not require data_source, consumer_family, or degraded_mode, which F001/F004 need for validation and per-family degradation checks.

The no-secret assertion is pinned only for the MCP transcript path, while the required evidence asks harness tests for all three agent adapters to be no-secret. CLI and contract artifacts could leak secret-shaped fields without violating the written F003 acceptance.

F004 describes a pure checker mostly at the journey evidence-set level, but the contract requires human and agent journeys for the same objective to agree by shared data_source key. The objective-level collection and comparison boundary is not pinned.

EvidenceRef data_provenance is optional for compatibility, but F002 does not define how consumer-readiness evidence with an evidence_class and missing data_provenance is handled. That leaves seeded-versus-real enforcement dependent on implementation choices.
